observations.trace: The page runner orders updater, batching, non-compute output writes, page flush, then page update. The updater requests source and output capacity for the same allocator watermark, preserves source during reallocation, and leaves output copying disabled. lens_perspectives.assessment: Input instance length is narrowed for native allocation while the full input is carried into source upload; their connected size domain requires explicit admission.
Native InstanceAllocation couples page and offset, while Write carries entity, offset and batch identity; an index type does not by itself validate the count/upload extent.
Count conversion, allocator success and buffer/device capacity require caller conditions; the ordinary zero-length path is separately filtered by native collection.
Page counters, watermark, pending clears, capacity alignment, upload length and reset are related operations; known reset/copy questions remain distinct.
Page buffers, bind groups and batch tables must agree on one logical page; normal runner ordering is scoped evidence, not proof for arbitrary public state.
Native allocator owns page/slot protocol, renderer owns upload and culling, and 95e current chunk instancing is a separate first-party renderer.
Watermark and active count serve related but different roles; leaving active counts behind on global reset is the earlier conditional coherence issue.
Future native-boundary work should preserve source copy on growth, valid output regeneration policy, empty-page semantics and target-specific draw protocol after policy is determined.
Default Paged and Custom backends are distinct closed variants; no blanket claim that custom allocators share paged invariants.
Derives and macros were inspected as source only. No expansion or inferred replacement of native trait or resource logic.
Page ID, instance count, element offset, byte capacity, batch ID and tombstone marker have different meanings despite u32/u64 storage.
Formatting buffer labels is an open diagnostic boundary; no domain lookup or hard-coded application identity was established.
Four-byte alignment, 1024-byte minimum and invalid-batch sentinel are native buffer/format parameters; u32 narrowing is a representability boundary, not gameplay tuning.
